dropped.claim: EVI Industries is a value-added distributor of commercial laundry equipment serving approximately 55,000 customers across North America and Latin America with no customer concentration risk. The company pursues a debt-funded 'buy-and-build' acquisition strategy but has shown deteriorating operating leverage: despite growing revenue 10.3% to $389.8M in FY 2025, operating income of $13.8M remains 16% below the $16.5M achieved in FY 2023, while net income of $7.5M lags the $9.7M earned two years earlier. Long-term debt surged from $12.9M to $53.0M to fund four FY 2025 acquisitions, yet operating cash flow declined from $32.7M to $21.3M, and covenant constraints leave only $56.1M available under a $150M credit facility. With operating margin of just 3.5%, return on equity of 5.2%, and SG&A expenses rising as a percentage of revenue despite double-digit growth, the acquisition strategy appears to be destroying rather than creating value.

dropped.claim: EVI Industries presents a textbook case of value destruction through acquisitions. Despite 13.4% three-year revenue CAGR, operating income remains below FY 2023 levels, operating margins are anemic at 3.5%, and return on equity is a dismal 5.2%. The company consumed $50.6M in cash for acquisitions while operating cash flow declined 35%, requiring debt to surge from $12.9M to $53.0M. Most critically, the company exhibits negative operating leverage—SG&A as a percentage of revenue increased despite double-digit growth—suggesting acquired businesses are less profitable than the base business and integration is failing. With only $56.1M borrowing capacity remaining under covenant constraints and the 'buy-and-build' strategy explicitly central to management's plans, the company faces a strategic dead end: it cannot profitably integrate what it has bought and has limited capacity to buy more. The 47x P/E ratio appears divorced from the underlying economics of a low-margin, cash-consumptive distribution business trading at 1.0x sales.

Operating profitability deteriorated despite revenue growth, with operating income of $13.8M in FY 2025 remaining 16% below the $16.5M achieved in FY 2023 and net income of $7.5M still 23% below the $9.7M earned two years earlier, suggesting the acquisition strategy is destroying value.
